title: Well-initialized Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (WLTH)
content: Well-initialized Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (WLTH): "A well-initialized dense neural network contains globally minimal solutions that can retain the prior class knowledge while providing room to learn the new class knowledge through isolated fine-tuning of the networks or subnetworks." WLTH posits that when starting from a well-pretrained (well-initialized) transformer backbone, there exist per-task subnetworks or task-adaptive soft-networks that (i) preserve previously learned classes and (ii) admit isolated fine-tuning to learn new classes without catastrophic forgetting.

title: Soft-TransFormers (Soft-TF): algorithm and operational definition
content:
Soft-TransFormers (Soft-TF) is a method that (a) keeps pre-trained transformer parameters $\boldsymbol{\theta}$ frozen and (b) learns per-task task-adaptive soft-parameters $\boldsymbol{m}_t$ (real-valued masks applied elementwise) together with shared G-prompts $\boldsymbol{g}$, task E-prompts $\{\boldsymbol{e}_t\}$, task keys $\{\boldsymbol{k}_t\}$, and a task classifier $f_{\phi}$. The method instantiates a soft-MSA layer by applying masks to projection matrices so that a multi-head attention projection $\boldsymbol{w}^{O},\boldsymbol{w}_{i}^{Q},\boldsymbol{w}_{i}^{K},\boldsymbol{w}_{i}^{V}$ is used in computation as $\boldsymbol{w}^{O}\odot \boldsymbol{m}^{O}$ and $\boldsymbol{w}_i^{Q}\odot \boldsymbol{m}^Q$, etc., producing $ \operatorname{MSA}(\boldsymbol{h}_Q,\boldsymbol{h}_K,\boldsymbol{h}_V)=\operatorname{Concat}(\boldsymbol{h}_1,\dots,\boldsymbol{h}_n)\;(\boldsymbol{w}^{O}\odot \boldsymbol{m}^{O}) $ with $\boldsymbol{h}_i=\operatorname{Attention}(\boldsymbol{h}_Q(\boldsymbol{w}_i^{Q}\odot \boldsymbol{m}^Q),\boldsymbol{h}_K(\boldsymbol{w}_i^{K}\odot \boldsymbol{m}^K),\boldsymbol{h}_V(\boldsymbol{w}_i^{V}\odot \boldsymbol{m}^V))$. Training optimizes
      $$
      \min_{\boldsymbol{g},\boldsymbol{e}_t,\boldsymbol{m}_t,\boldsymbol{k}_t,\phi}\; \mathcal{L}\big(f_{\phi}(f_{\boldsymbol{g},\boldsymbol{e}_t,\boldsymbol{m}_t}(\boldsymbol{x})),y\big)+\lambda\mathcal{L}_{\text{match}}(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{k}_t),\quad \boldsymbol{x}\in\mathcal{D}_t,
      $$
      where $\mathcal{L}$ is cross-entropy and $\mathcal{L}_{\text{match}}(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{k}_t)=\gamma(q(\boldsymbol{x}),\boldsymbol{k}_t)$ is cosine matching of the [class] token feature $q(\boldsymbol{x})$. During training for each task $t$, the task-specific E-prompt $\boldsymbol{e}_t$, soft-network $\boldsymbol{m}_t$, and task key $\boldsymbol{k}_t$ are selected; the shared G-prompt $\boldsymbol{g}$ and $\boldsymbol{e}_t$ are attached to the designated layers; and all learnable parameters $\phi$, $\boldsymbol{g}$, $\boldsymbol{E}$, $\boldsymbol{M}$, $\boldsymbol{K}$ are updated by backpropagation on the loss. At test time, task inference is performed either by Prompt ID ($\arg\min_t \gamma(q(\boldsymbol{x}),\boldsymbol{k}_t)$) or Gradient ID (one-shot inference by computing $\hat t=\arg\min_t \partial \mathcal{H}/\partial \alpha_t$ with $\alpha_t$ mixing weights over learned subnetworks, where $\mathcal{H}$ is the entropy function). After task inference, the corresponding E-prompt $\boldsymbol{e}_{\hat t}$ and subnetwork $\boldsymbol{m}_{\hat t}$ are attached together with $\boldsymbol{g}$ to form the prompted architecture for prediction.

title: Convergence bound for Soft-TransFormers under convex-Lipschitz assumptions
content:
The convergence analysis considers a convex-Lipschitz loss function $f$ with gradient norm bounded by $\rho$, i.e., $\|\boldsymbol{v}_t\|\le \rho$ for per-iteration gradient vectors $\boldsymbol{v}_t$, and an update rule $\boldsymbol{w}^{(t+1)}=\boldsymbol{w}^{(t)}-\eta\boldsymbol{v}_t$ applied sequentially over $T$ steps. Define $\overline{\boldsymbol{w}}=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T\boldsymbol{w}^{(t)}$ and let $\boldsymbol{w}^*$ be any comparator vector. Let $\boldsymbol{w}_m$ denote the effective weighted parameters when masks $\boldsymbol{m}$ are applied, e.g., $\boldsymbol{w}_m=(\boldsymbol{w}^Q\odot\boldsymbol{m}^Q)\,\boldsymbol{x}\boldsymbol{p}^T\,(\boldsymbol{w}^K\odot\boldsymbol{m}^K)^T$, where $\boldsymbol{x}$ is the image token embedding and $\boldsymbol{p}$ is the prompt token embedding from the concatenated input $\boldsymbol{z}=[\boldsymbol{p};\boldsymbol{x}]$, and $\boldsymbol{w}^Q,\boldsymbol{w}^K$ are frozen pre-trained projection matrices. Let $\boldsymbol{w}_p$ denote the prompt-only effective parameters (with $\boldsymbol{m}=\mathbf{1}$). For any $B_m< B_p < B$, where $B_m=\|\boldsymbol{w}_m^{(T+1)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*\|$, $B_p=\|\boldsymbol{w}_p^{(T+1)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*\|$, and $\|\boldsymbol{w}^{(T+1)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*\|\le B$, choosing $\eta=\sqrt{B^2/(\rho^2 T)}$ yields the bound
      $$
      \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T\langle \boldsymbol{w}^{(t)}-\boldsymbol{w}^*,\boldsymbol{v}_t\rangle \le \frac{B_m\rho}{\sqrt{T}} < \frac{B_p\rho}{\sqrt{T}} < \frac{B\rho}{\sqrt{T}}.
      $$
      Consequently, the sub-optimality $f(\overline{\boldsymbol{w}})-f(\boldsymbol{w}^*)$ is upper-bounded by quantities that scale as $\mathcal{O}(B_m\rho/\sqrt{T})$, where a smaller $B_m$ (associated with learning soft masks) yields a tighter bound than prompt-only or unconstrained updates.

title: Soft-TF achieves state-of-the-art continual-learning performance on ViT benchmarks
content: On ViT-based continual-learning benchmarks Soft-TF obtains state-of-the-art (SOTA) class-incremental and task-incremental results. Representative results: DualPrompt-Soft-TF (using Gradient ID) on 10-Split-CIFAR100 achieves ACC = 97.87% and Forget = 0.21; on 20-Split-CIFAR100 ACC = 99.05% and Forget = 0.24; on 10-Split-ImageNet-R ACC = 82.38% and Forget = 0.59. These results substantially outperform prompt-only baselines (e.g., DualPrompt with Prompt ID: ACC=86.50%, Forget=5.77; L2P-PGP: ACC=84.34%, Forget=5.59; L2P: ACC=83.77%, Forget=6.63) and rehearsal/regularization baselines (e.g., BiC with 5,000 exemplars: ACC=81.42%, Forget=17.31; EWC: ACC=47.01%, Forget=33.27) on 10-Split-CIFAR100.

title: Soft-TF extends to CLIP and yields strong CIL/TIL results
content: Soft-TF generalizes to vision-language backbones (CLIP). On 10-Split-CIFAR100 with CLIP backbone, CLIP-Prompt-Soft-TF-L[1-12] using Gradient ID attains CIL ACC = 85.90% and Forget = 3.07, and TIL ACC = 96.83% and Forget = 0.44, showing substantial improvement over CLIP prompt baselines (CLIP with Prompt ID: CIL ACC=73.76%, Forget=5.60; CLIP-PGP: CIL ACC=79.47%, Forget=4.23) under the same task settings.

title: Layer-wise and attention-only ablations identify effective fine-tuning loci
content: Empirical ablations show that (a) applying Soft-TF to higher transformer layers (e.g., layers L[10,11,12]) yields stronger continual-learning performance in DualPrompt settings, producing near-zero forgetting (example: DualPrompt-Soft-TF-L[10,11,12] Gradient ID ACC = 97.87%, Forget = 0.21), and (b) fine-tuning only attention projections (QKV and projection matrices) at last layers (Soft-TF-L[12] w/ only ATTN) already attains very high performance (reported ACC = 97.17%, Forget = 0.40 in one configuration), indicating that attention modules (especially QKV) are highly influential for task-adaptive specialization.

title: Transformer sparse subnetworks (WSN-style) exist and yield competitive CF behavior
content: Extending WSN-style subnetworks to pre-trained transformers yields competitive sparse solutions: e.g., DualPrompt-WSN-L[10,11,12] with sparsity c=87.0% on 10-Split-TinyImageNet achieves ACC=91.91% and Forget=0.38. This empirical observation supports a "rotary" or transformer's lottery-like phenomenon (authors term Rottary Ticket Hypothesis, RTH) where dense pretrained transformers contain high-performing sparse subnetworks.
